title: Owner only plus group read
prompt: Give the file deploy.sh these permissions: the owner can read, write and run it; the group can read and run it; everyone else gets nothing. Type the command.
hints: Permissions are three digits: owner, group, others.
Read is 4, write is 2, execute is 1. Add them up for each digit.
Owner 4+2+1, group 4+1, others 0.

title: Biggest memory users
prompt: Show the five processes that use the most memory, biggest first. Use ps and head. Type the command.
hints: ps can sort its output with --sort. A minus sign means biggest first.
The header line counts as one, so ask head for six lines.

title: Which folder is eating /var
prompt: List the folders directly under /var with their sizes, biggest first. Type the command.
hints: du -sh prints a summary size in human form for each path you give it.
Give it /var/* and sort the result: sort -h understands sizes such as 12M.
Add -r to sort so the biggest is first.

title: Follow the ssh service log
prompt: Show the last 50 lines of the journal for the ssh service and keep following new lines. Type the command.
hints: journalctl reads the systemd journal.
-u picks a unit, -n sets the number of lines, -f follows.

title: Fix the backup schedule
prompt: This crontab line runs every night. Change it so the backup runs every Monday at 03:30 and adds its output (normal and error) to /var/log/backup.log.

rules.msg: The time fields should be minute 30, hour 3, any day of month, any month, Monday.
Send errors to the same place with 2>&1.

hints: Cron fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
Monday is 1 in the last field.
Redirect with: >> file 2>&1

title: Harden sshd
prompt: Edit these sshd settings so root cannot log in and passwords are not accepted (keys only).
starter:
PermitRootLogin yes
PasswordAuthentication yes
PubkeyAuthentication yes

rules.msg: Keep PubkeyAuthentication yes, or you lock yourself out.

hints: Each setting is a keyword and a value on one line.
Keep key login on, or nobody can get in.
solution:
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes

title: Undo the last commit, keep the work
prompt: Undo the last commit but keep all its changes staged. Type the command.
hints: git reset moves the branch pointer back.
--soft keeps your changes staged; --hard would throw them away.

title: Create and switch
prompt: Create a branch called fix/login and switch to it in one command. Type the command.
hints: Both git switch and git checkout can do this.
Look for the flag that creates the branch.

title: Squash three commits
prompt: Start an interactive rebase to tidy the last three commits. Type the command.
hints: Interactive rebase is rebase -i.
Count back from HEAD.

title: Annotated release tag
prompt: Create an annotated tag v1.4.0 with the message "Release 1.4.0". Type the command.
hints: -a makes an annotated tag.
-m gives the message in quotes.

title: First push of a branch
prompt: Push the current branch to origin and remember it as the upstream. Type the command.
hints: The remote is named origin.
-u links the local branch to the remote one.

title: Make the script stop on errors
prompt: This script keeps going after a failure and uses an unquoted variable. Make it stop on errors, on unset variables and in failed pipelines, and quote the variable.

rules.msg: Add set -euo pipefail near the top.

hints: Strict mode is one line after the shebang.
Quotes stop spaces in a name from splitting the word.

title: Count unique visitors
prompt: access.log has the client address in the first field. Count the unique addresses with awk, sort and wc. Type the command.
hints: awk can print one field of each line.
sort -u keeps unique lines; wc -l counts lines.

title: A default value
prompt: Print the value of APP_ENV, or the word dev if APP_ENV is unset or empty. Type the echo command.
hints: Parameter expansion has a default form with :-
The form is ${NAME:-default}.

title: Quote the loop
prompt: This loop breaks on file names with spaces. Fix it by quoting the variable and reading the glob directly.
starter:
for f in $(ls *.log); do
  gzip $f
done

rules.msg: Do not parse ls. Use for f in *.log.
Loop over the glob: for f in *.log

hints: ls output is split on spaces.
A glob expands to separate words safely.
solution:
for f in *.log; do
  gzip "$f"
done

title: A safe HTTP call
prompt: Make this call safe: add a 5 second timeout and stop with an error on a bad status.
starter:
import requests
r = requests.get(url)
data = r.json()

rules.msg: Add timeout=5 to the get call.
Call r.raise_for_status() before reading the body.

hints: Without a timeout, a call can wait forever.
raise_for_status turns 4xx and 5xx into an exception.
solution:
import requests
r = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
r.raise_for_status()
data = r.json()

title: Use logging, not print
prompt: Replace the print calls with the logging module: log the start as info and the failure as error.

rules.msg: Import and use the logging module.
Log the failure with error or exception.

hints: logging has levels: debug, info, warning, error.
logging.exception logs the traceback too.

title: Close the file
prompt: Rewrite this so the file is always closed, even on errors, and read it as UTF-8.

rules.msg: The with block closes the file; remove close().

hints: with ... as f: closes the file for you.
open() takes an encoding argument.
solution:
with open("data.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    text = f.read()

title: Hosts in a /26
prompt: How many usable host addresses are in a /26 network? Type the number.
hints: A /26 leaves 6 host bits.
2 to the power 6, minus the network and broadcast addresses.

title: Find the mail servers
prompt: Ask DNS for the mail (MX) records of example.com using dig. Type the command.
hints: dig takes a name and a record type.
The record type for mail is MX.

title: Who is listening
prompt: Show listening TCP sockets with numeric ports and the owning process. Type the ss command.
hints: ss replaces netstat.
Flags: t for TCP, l for listening, n for numbers, p for process.

title: Only the headers
prompt: Show only the response headers of https://example.com with curl. Type the command.
hints: curl can send a HEAD request.
The short flag is a capital I.

title: A safer Dockerfile
prompt: Improve this Dockerfile: pin the base image to a specific version (not latest), and run as a non-root user.

rules.msg: Do not use the latest tag.
Pin a version tag, for example ubuntu:24.04.
Add a USER line with a non-root user.

hints: A tag such as 24.04 is repeatable; latest changes over time.
USER switches the user for later steps and the container.
solution:
FROM ubuntu:24.04
RUN useradd -r app
COPY app /app
USER app
CMD ["/app/run"]

title: Run a web server
prompt: Run nginx in the background, name it web, and publish host port 8080 to container port 80. Type the command.
hints: -d runs it detached; --name names it.
-p host:container publishes a port.

title: Keep the database data
prompt: Run postgres with a named volume called pgdata mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data. Type the command.
hints: A named volume is name:path with -v.
The image name comes last.

title: Limit memory and CPU
prompt: Run nginx with at most 256 MB of memory and half a CPU. Type the command.
hints: Memory flag: --memory 256m.
CPU flag: --cpus 0.5.

title: Restart and health
prompt: Add a restart policy that keeps the service running unless you stop it, and a health check that runs curl -f http://localhost every 30 seconds.

rules.msg: The test should run curl -f http://localhost.

hints: Both belong under the web service.
healthcheck has test, interval, timeout and retries.
solution:
services:
  web:
    image: nginx:1.27
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost"]
      interval: 30s

title: Scale a deployment
prompt: Scale the deployment web to 5 replicas. Type the kubectl command.
hints: kubectl scale changes the replica count.
Name the resource kind and name, then --replicas.

title: Probes and limits
prompt: Add a readiness probe (HTTP GET / on port 80) and resource requests and limits to the container.
starter:
containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:1.27
    ports:
      - containerPort: 80

rules.msg: The probe should use httpGet on path / and port 80.

hints: Probes sit at the same level as image and ports.
resources has requests and limits, each with cpu and memory.
solution:
containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:1.27
    ports:
      - containerPort: 80
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /
        port: 80
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 128Mi
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 256Mi

title: Expose a deployment
prompt: Create a ClusterIP service for deployment web that listens on port 80 and sends traffic to container port 8080. Type the command.
hints: kubectl expose creates a service for a workload.
Two port flags: --port and --target-port.

title: Make a secret
prompt: Create a generic secret named db-pass with the key password and the value s3cret. Type the command.
hints: The type of secret is generic.
--from-literal takes key=value.

title: Why is it Pending
prompt: Show the events and details for the pod web-7d so you can see why it is Pending. Type the command.
hints: describe shows events at the bottom.
The resource kind is pod.

title: Logs of the crashed container
prompt: Show the logs of the previous (crashed) container of pod web-7d. Type the command.
hints: A restarted container has a previous instance.
The flag is --previous (or -p).

title: Can jane delete pods
prompt: Ask the API whether the user jane can delete pods in the namespace prod. Type the command.
hints: kubectl auth can-i answers yes or no.
--as impersonates a user.
solution: kubectl auth can-i delete pods --as jane -n prod

title: Autoscale a deployment
prompt: Autoscale deployment web between 2 and 10 replicas at 70 percent CPU. Type the command.
hints: kubectl autoscale creates a HorizontalPodAutoscaler.
Flags: --min, --max and a CPU target.

title: Ask for 5 GiB
prompt: Complete this claim: it needs 5 GiB of storage and can be mounted read-write by one node.
starter:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data
spec:
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
hints: accessModes is a list under spec.
ReadWriteOnce means one node at a time.
solution:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi

title: Nightly job
prompt: Set the CronJob to run every day at 02:00 and never run two copies at once.
starter:
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
hints: Cron fields: minute hour day month weekday.
concurrencyPolicy sits next to schedule.
solution:
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure

title: Install with a value
prompt: Install the chart bitnami/nginx as release web in the namespace prod (create it if needed) with replicaCount set to 3. Type the helm command.
hints: helm install takes a release name and a chart.
--set changes one value; --create-namespace makes the namespace.
solution: helm install web bitnami/nginx --set replicaCount=3 -n prod --create-namespace

title: Go back to revision 2
prompt: Roll the release web back to revision 2. Type the command.
hints: helm history lists revisions.
helm rollback takes the release and a revision number.

title: Render without installing
prompt: Render the chart in ./chart with the file values.yaml and print the YAML without installing anything. Type the command.
hints: helm template renders locally.
Give a release name, the chart path, and -f for the values file.

title: List what Terraform manages
prompt: List every resource in the Terraform state. Type the command.
hints: The state subcommand has a list action.
Run terraform state with nothing after it to see the actions.

title: Save the plan
prompt: Save a plan to a file called tfplan so you can apply exactly that plan later. Type the command.
hints: terraform plan can write its result to a file.
The flag is -out.

title: A checked variable
prompt: Give this variable a description and a validation that only allows the values dev, test and prod.
hints: validation has a condition and an error_message.
contains(list, value) returns true or false.

title: Rename without destroying
prompt: You renamed aws_instance.web to aws_instance.app in the code. Add a block that tells Terraform it is the same object.
starter: # resource renamed from web to app
hints: The block is called moved.
It has from and to, both resource addresses.

title: Hide an output
prompt: Mark this output so Terraform does not print its value.
hints: Outputs accept a sensitive argument.
It is a true or false value inside the output block.

title: Request rate
prompt: Write a PromQL expression for the per-second rate of http_requests_total averaged over 5 minutes.
hints: Counters only go up; use rate().
A range selector looks like [5m].

title: Error ratio
prompt: Write a PromQL expression for the share of requests with a 5xx status over 5 minutes: errors divided by all requests.
hints: Divide the rate of 5xx requests by the rate of all requests.
Match 5xx with status=~"5..".

title: A calmer alert
prompt: Make this alert wait ten minutes before firing, label it as a page, and add a summary.
hints: for: goes next to expr.
labels and annotations are maps.
solution:
- alert: HighErrorRate
  expr: error_ratio > 0.05
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "More than 5 percent of requests fail"

title: Error budget in minutes
prompt: An SLO of 99.9 percent over 30 days allows how many minutes of downtime? Type the number.
hints: 30 days is 43,200 minutes.
The budget is 0.1 percent of that.

title: Requests per second
prompt: 100 million requests per day is about how many requests per second on average? Type a number.
hints: A day has 86,400 seconds.

title: A locked-down container
prompt: Add a security context that runs as non-root, blocks privilege escalation and makes the file system read-only.
hints: securityContext is a field of the container.
Three booleans do the job.
solution:
containers:
  - name: app
    image: app:1.0
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

title: Idempotent install
prompt: Replace the shell command with a module that only changes the server when nginx is missing.
starter:
- name: install nginx
  shell: apt-get install -y nginx

rules.msg: Do not use shell for this.
Use the apt or package module.
Set name: nginx for the module.

hints: Modules describe the end state.
apt takes name and state.
solution:
- name: install nginx
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: nginx
    state: present

title: Index a column
prompt: Create an index called idx_orders_customer on the orders table for the customer_id column. Type the SQL.
hints: CREATE INDEX name ON table (column).
The index name is idx_orders_customer, the table is orders.

title: See the real plan
prompt: Run a query on orders and show the real execution plan with timings. Type the SQL (any simple select).
hints: EXPLAIN shows the plan; ANALYZE runs it and times it.
Put both words before a normal SELECT.
solution: EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42;

title: Least privilege
prompt: This policy allows everything. Allow only reading objects (s3:GetObject) from the bucket reports-bucket.
hints: Name the action and the resource.
An S3 object ARN looks like arn:aws:s3:::bucket/*

title: Snapshot etcd
prompt: Save an etcd snapshot to /backup/etcd.db with etcdctl. Type the command (certificate flags are not needed here).
hints: etcdctl has a snapshot subcommand.
snapshot save takes the output path.

title: Drain a node
prompt: Safely drain node worker-1: ignore daemon sets and allow deleting pods that use emptyDir. Type the command.
hints: kubectl drain evicts the pods.
Two flags are almost always needed.

title: Sync an app
prompt: Ask Argo CD to sync the application web from the command line. Type the command.
hints: argocd app has sync, get and diff.
Give the action and then the application name.

title: Ask for JSON only
prompt: Rewrite this prompt so the model answers with JSON only, using the keys "severity" and "summary", and gets one example.

rules.msg: Say "only" so there is no extra text.

hints: Say what format, which keys, and show one example.
Use the word only.

title: A clear tool definition
prompt: Give this tool a description that says when to use it and a required string parameter named city.

rules.msg: Add a description of at least 20 characters.

hints: Tools have name, description and an input schema.
The schema lists properties and required names.
